description: The feature set the released penguin-qemu artifact is built with. Ported from rehosting/qemu build.sh at origin/main 56554982a8 (the VNC/modules and block/USB/compression/capstone commits).
schemaNote: configureArgs entries are objects, not strings: `flag` is passed to configure, `why` carries the rationale that lived in build.sh's comments, and `nixDeps` names the nixpkgs attributes that flag needs. nix/qemu.nix derives buildInputs from nixDeps, so the two lists cannot drift -- rehosting/qemu's nix/qemu.nix has a comment asking a human to keep them in sync by hand.

configureArgs.why: Modules must stay OFF: scripts/penguin-qemu-package.py ships only the libqemu-*.so libraries, never QEMU's module directory. With modules enabled, anything meson chooses to modularise (notably virtio-gpu) was built but never packaged, so `-device virtio-gpu` failed at runtime with "not a valid device model name". Building in costs ~36 KB/arch.
Required: the softmmu objects get relinked into shared libraries.

VNC is the only display backend we ship: it needs no host display, and its only hard dependency is pixman, which we already have (meson.build's `vnc = declare_dependency()` is a dummy). Costs ~141 KB/arch and zero new store paths. Its optional extras are pinned off rather than left on auto so the build can't silently acquire deps if buildInputs ever grow.
libjpeg (tight encoding) is cheap against the image and directly improves VNC.
penguin authenticates VNC with password-secret, so the SASL auth path would be an unused parser.
dbus-display auto-enables off glib alone, which IS in our buildInputs. Pin it off so it cannot drift in unnoticed.
QEMU's own disassembler (pkg-config, >=3.0.5). The one genuinely new dependency at ~29 MB -- the penguin image ships only the Python binding, not the C library.
Host block I/O performance only, and it changes I/O behaviour rather than adding a capability.

groupNote: The block/USB/compression/disassembler group is enabled deliberately, costed against the penguin image rather than against this package alone: every library is either already in the image (curl, lzo, bzip2, libpng, libjpeg) or under ~5 MB marginal (libiscsi, libnfs, rdma-core, libusb1, usbredir). These are HARD enables, so a missing library is a configure failure, not a silent downgrade.
